LESSON: GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS (GIS)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Practical Geography
Topic 1.4: Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Geographic Information Systems (GIS), part of Practical Geography in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: how is geospatial technology useful to humans? 2. how can we use gps in locating places in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Geographic Information Systems (GIS) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: The skill of sharing learnt knowledge is promoted as the learner converts geographic coordinates and

present in class

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology is enhanced as the learner uses digital resources with assistive

technology to locate points on the earth’s surface

Values:
● Responsibility: Learner offers leadership and guidance to others as they use print or digital resources with assistive

technology to research on the importance of GIS in geographical studies

● Respect: Learner displays open-mindedness as they discuss the components of GIS

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social Cohesion: Learner works with others as they discuss the components of GIS.

● Critical Thinking: Learner creates a poster on the importance of GIS in geographical studies.

● Self-Awareness: Learner uses digital resources with assistive technology to locate points on the earth’s surface.

Suggested Learning Resources

Local and extended environment, Digitizers, Maps, Tactile Maps, Digital devices with assistive technology, Approved

textbooks and other relevant resources, Display boards, Wall charts, Flip charts, Whiteboards and marker pens, tactile posters

or banners.

Suggested Key Skills

• Analysing the branches of Geography for in-depth understanding of the subject.

12

• Exploring the relationship between Geography and other disciplines for identification of career pathways.

• Interpreting relief, drainage and vegetation on topographical maps for resource mapping.

• Drawing or describing tactile sketch sections presented in appropriate print or tactile format from topographical maps for

interpreting relief.

• Examining the methods of data collection, analysis and presentation in geographical studies.

• Collect, analyzing, interpreting and presenting statistical data in a Geographical phenomenon.

• Describing components of GIS as used in geo-referencing information.

• Applying GIS in locating the position of the school.
